answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. memory_31 and memory_86 directly demonstrated that simplifying onboarding and shortening flows improve completion rates and early activation. These are proven levers in our playbook. Verifying both will confirm the durability of these effects and any relevant context about SMB vs broader segments. While memory_73 shows promotional pricing can drive short-term revenue, it carries documented retention risk (12-point weakness in later-cycle). Given the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, the retention trade-off is material. memory_57 (referral incentives) works well but requires established customer base—won't address the immediate activation decline. memory_44 (enterprise sales assist) is valuable but orthogonal to the current SMB-driven competitive pressure. Simplifying onboarding addresses both metrics simultaneously, leverages proven playbook elements, and poses lower downstream risk. The standard experiment scale allows confidence-building before broader rollout, preserving our ability to pivot if unexpected effects emerge.
